Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: The company maintains information security policies that define security roles, responsibilities and requirements. Policies are approved by management and reviewed at least annually.
Evidence: Policy set; approval and version history.

Rule: All stages, when Governance is Formal committees.
Wording: A security committee meets at least quarterly under a documented charter to oversee the security and compliance programme. Minutes record decisions and actions.
Evidence: Committee charter; meeting minutes; action log.

Rule: All stages, when Governance isn't Formal committees (or isn't answered yet).
Control: Management review of the security programme
Wording: Management reviews the status of the security and compliance programme at least semi-annually, and decisions and actions are recorded.
Evidence: Review notes or minutes with date, attendees and actions.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: The company maintains an organisational chart that shows reporting lines, and updates it as the structure changes.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Control: Code of conduct and disciplinary policy
Wording: A code of conduct sets out expected behaviour and the disciplinary process for breaches.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: An acceptable use policy sets out how personnel may use company systems, devices and data.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Personnel acknowledge the code of conduct and information security policies when they join and at least annually.
Evidence: Acknowledgement records for new and existing personnel.

Rule: Scaleup and Enterprise. Always included.
Wording: A named security lead is accountable for the security programme, and their responsibilities are documented.

Rule: Enterprise only. Always included.
Wording: The board of directors, or an equivalent governing body, receives a security and compliance update at least annually and exercises oversight independently of management.

Rule: Enterprise only. Always included.
Wording: Exceptions to security policies are risk-assessed, approved by management, time-limited and tracked to closure.

Rule: Enterprise only. Always included.
Wording: An independent review of the control environment (internal audit or a second-line function) is performed at least annually, and findings are tracked to resolution.

Rule: Enterprise only. Always included.
Wording: Security and compliance metrics are reported to management at least monthly.

Rule: All stages, when a Compliance Automation tool is named.
Wording: {{TOOL}} continuously monitors configuration controls across in-scope systems, and failing tests are assigned an owner and remediated.

Rule: All stages, when Control execution is Automated / agentic or Hybrid.
Control: Oversight of automated and agent-run controls
Wording: Each automated or agent-run control has a named owner. Failures and exceptions are escalated for human review, and changes to the control's logic or permissions are approved before use.
Evidence: Automation inventory with owners; exception queue; change approvals.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Background checks are performed on new personnel before they start, where permitted by law.
Evidence: Background check results for new hires.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Personnel complete security awareness training when they join and at least annually.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Personnel and contractors sign confidentiality agreements before they are given access to company systems.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Personnel receive a performance evaluation at least annually.

Rule: Scaleup and Enterprise, when a Code Repository tool is named.
Wording: Engineers complete secure development training when they join and at least annually.

Rule: Scaleup and Enterprise. Always included.
Wording: Phishing simulations are run at least quarterly, and personnel who fail receive follow-up training.

Rule: Enterprise only. Always included.
Wording: Job descriptions document the responsibilities and security expectations of each role, including those with access to sensitive systems.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: A risk management policy defines how risks, including fraud risk, are identified, assessed, treated and monitored.

Rule: All stages, when Risk management isn't Continuous (or isn't answered yet).
Wording: A risk assessment, including fraud risk and changes to the business, is performed at least annually and recorded in the risk register.

Rule: All stages, when Risk management is Continuous.
Wording: Risks are added to and updated in the risk register as they arise through operating processes (changes, incidents, vendor reviews), and management reviews the full register, including fraud risk, at least annually.
Evidence: Risk register history; annual review record.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Each identified risk has an owner and a treatment decision, and residual risk is accepted by management.
Evidence: Risk register with owners, treatments and acceptance.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: The control framework maps controls to risks and requirements, and is reviewed at least annually and when the business or systems change.

Rule: Enterprise only. Always included.
Wording: Management defines a risk appetite statement, approved by the board, that guides risk acceptance decisions.

Rule: All stages, when Vendor management isn't Federated or Distributed (or isn't answered yet).
Wording: New vendors are assessed and approved before they handle company or customer data, and a central vendor inventory records each vendor's data access and criticality.

Rule: All stages, when Vendor management is Federated or Distributed.
Wording: Vendor owners assess new vendors against the company's vendor standard before they handle company or customer data, and record each vendor's data access and criticality in the central vendor inventory.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Critical vendors and subservice organisations are reviewed at least annually, including their independent assurance reports and the complementary controls the company must operate.
Evidence: Assurance reports; review records; CUEC mapping.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Agreements with vendors that handle customer data include security, confidentiality and, where relevant, data protection terms.

Rule: Enterprise only. Always included.
Wording: Critical vendors' security posture is monitored continuously, and material changes trigger a reassessment.

Rule: All stages, when a Infrastructure tool is named.
Wording: The company documents the controls it relies on from {{TOOL}} and reviews its independent assurance report at least annually, including the complementary controls the company must operate.

Rule: All stages, when a Hosting Platform tool is named, and no Infrastructure tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: The company documents the controls it relies on from {{TOOL}} and reviews its independent assurance report at least annually, including the complementary controls the company must operate.

Rule: All stages, when Access ownership is Centralised.
Wording: Access to in-scope systems is requested, approved by the manager or system owner, and provisioned centrally before use.
Evidence: Access requests and approvals; user listings with creation dates.

Rule: All stages, when Access ownership isn't Centralised (or isn't answered yet).
Wording: Access to in-scope systems is approved by the designated system owner before it is provisioned, following the company's access standard.
Evidence: Access requests and approvals; user listings with creation dates.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Access to in-scope systems is removed within one business day of a person leaving the company.

Rule: All stages, when a HR System tool is named.
Wording: Joiner, mover and leaver events in {{TOOL}} trigger account creation, changes and removal, and HR records are the source for access reviews and leaver checks.
Evidence: HR event reports matched to account changes.

Rule: All stages, when Access ownership is Centralised.
Wording: User access to in-scope systems is reviewed centrally with system owners at least quarterly, and inappropriate access is removed.

Rule: All stages, when Access ownership isn't Centralised (or isn't answered yet).
Wording: System owners review user access to their in-scope systems at least quarterly against a central schedule, and inappropriate access is removed.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Access to in-scope systems is granted by role, based on least privilege.

Rule: All stages, when Privileged & production access isn't Temporary / elevated or JIT (or isn't answered yet).
Wording: Privileged access to production is limited to authorised personnel, and the list of privileged users is reviewed at least quarterly.

Rule: All stages, when Privileged & production access is Temporary / elevated.
Wording: Privileged access to production is granted only for a defined need, approved before use and removed when the need ends.

Rule: All stages, when Privileged & production access is JIT.
Wording: Privileged access to production is granted just in time through an approval workflow and expires automatically.

Rule: All stages, when a Privileged Access Management tool is named.
Wording: Privileged sessions to production are brokered through {{TOOL}}, which enforces approval and records session activity.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Multi-factor authentication is required for access to in-scope systems.

Rule: All stages, when a Identity and Authentication tool is named.
Wording: Access to in-scope systems is federated through {{TOOL}} using single sign-on wherever the system supports it.

Rule: All stages, when a Identity and Authentication tool is named.
Wording: {{TOOL}} enforces an authentication policy that requires multi-factor authentication for all users.

Rule: All stages, when a Password Manager tool is named.
Wording: Personnel store and share credentials in {{TOOL}}, the company's password manager.

Rule: All stages, when no Password Manager tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Password requirements are enforced for access to in-scope systems, and shared credentials are stored securely.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Each user has a unique account for in-scope systems, and shared or service accounts have a named owner.

Rule: All stages, when a Infrastructure tool is named.
Wording: {{TOOL}} root and break-glass accounts are protected with multi-factor authentication, are not used for routine work, and their use triggers an alert.
Evidence: Root account MFA; alert rule; usage log.

Rule: All stages, when Provider access to customer data is Routine.
Wording: Staff access to customer data is limited to roles that need it, is logged, and is reviewed at least quarterly.

Rule: All stages, when Provider access to customer data isn't Routine or Technically restricted (or isn't answered yet).
Control: Staff access to customer data (exception only)
Wording: Staff access customer data only for an approved support or incident case, and each access is recorded against the ticket or customer request.

Rule: All stages, when Provider access to customer data is Technically restricted.
Control: Staff access to customer data (technically restricted)
Wording: The architecture prevents staff from reading customer data in normal operations, and any break-glass access requires approval and is logged.

Rule: All stages, when Customer administration is Provider-managed or Shared.
Wording: Administrative changes the company makes in customer accounts are authorised by the customer, performed by authorised staff and logged.

Rule: Scaleup and Enterprise. Always included.
Wording: Service accounts and API keys are inventoried with an owner, restricted to the access they need and reviewed at least annually.

Rule: Enterprise only. Always included.
Wording: Conflicting duties, such as developing and approving the same change or requesting and approving the same access, are segregated or monitored.

Rule: All stages, when Infrastructure operations isn't Serverless (or isn't answered yet).
Wording: Network traffic to production is restricted by firewall rules or security groups that deny by default, and rules are reviewed at least annually.
Evidence: Firewall or security group rules; review record.

Rule: All stages, when Infrastructure operations is Serverless.
Wording: Production services are exposed only through managed endpoints (API gateways, load balancers or edge services) with restricted resource policies, reviewed at least annually.
Evidence: Endpoint and resource policy configuration; review record.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Control: No public access to data stores
Wording: Production data stores and administrative interfaces are not accessible from the public internet.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Data sent over public networks is encrypted using current TLS.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Customer data stored in production is encrypted at rest.

Rule: All stages, when a Application Secrets and Encryption tool is named.
Wording: Application secrets and encryption keys are stored in {{TOOL}}, access is restricted to authorised services and people, and keys are rotated at least annually.
Evidence: Secrets and key access policies; rotation history.

Rule: All stages, when no Application Secrets and Encryption tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Application secrets and encryption keys are kept out of source code in restricted configuration stores, and are rotated at least annually.

Rule: All stages, when a Edge and Web Protection tool is named.
Wording: Public traffic to the production application passes through {{TOOL}}, which enforces encrypted connections and web application firewall protection.

Rule: All stages, when a Databases tool is named.
Wording: {{TOOL}} production databases use encryption at rest and in transit, private network access and unique database users.

Rule: All stages, when Data control boundary is Customer-controlled or Shared.
Wording: Customers can choose where their data is stored, or manage their own encryption keys, and the company enforces those choices.
Evidence: Region or key configuration per customer.

Rule: All stages, when a Data Loss Prevention tool is named.
Wording: {{TOOL}} monitors for sensitive data leaving approved locations, and alerts are reviewed by responsible personnel.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: A data classification and handling policy defines data types and how each must be protected.

Rule: All stages, when Tenancy & isolation isn't Isolated or Dedicated (or isn't answered yet).
Wording: Customer data is logically segregated by tenant in the application and data layers, and segregation is tested at least annually.
Evidence: Data model; penetration test scope and results.

Rule: All stages, when Tenancy & isolation is Isolated.
Wording: Each customer's data is held in an isolated logical environment (separate schema, database or encryption key).

Rule: All stages, when Tenancy & isolation is Dedicated.
Wording: Each customer runs in a dedicated environment separated at the account or network level.
Evidence: Account or network structure per customer.

Rule: All stages, when a Device Management tool is named.
Wording: Company devices are enrolled in {{TOOL}}, which enforces disk encryption, screen lock, OS updates and the company's configuration baseline.

Rule: All stages, when no Device Management tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Company devices have disk encryption, screen lock and current OS updates, checked at least quarterly.

Rule: All stages, when a Endpoint Protection tool is named.
Wording: {{TOOL}} runs on company devices to detect and respond to malicious activity, and alerts go to responsible personnel.

Rule: All stages, when no Endpoint Protection tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Anti-malware protection (built-in OS protection is acceptable) is active on company devices, checked at least quarterly.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: An inventory of devices and production assets is maintained and reviewed at least annually.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Devices and media holding company data are securely wiped or destroyed before disposal or reuse.

Rule: All stages, when Endpoint model is BYOD or Mixed.
Wording: Personal devices used for work meet minimum security requirements and reach company data only through managed apps or browser sessions; personal devices cannot access production.

Rule: Enterprise only, when Endpoint model isn't BYOD (or isn't answered yet).
Wording: Only managed devices that meet the configuration baseline can access in-scope systems.

Values: Office(s) with in-scope equipment|On-premises data centre / server room|Manufacturing / production site|Warehouse / logistics site
Rule: All stages, when Facilities is Office(s) with in-scope equipment, On-premises data centre / server room, Manufacturing / production site or Warehouse / logistics site.
Wording: Physical access to areas with in-scope equipment is restricted to authorised people, visitors are escorted, and access rights are reviewed at least annually.
Evidence: Badge access list; visitor log; review record.

Rule: All stages, when Facilities is Customer sites (company devices deployed).
Wording: Company devices deployed at customer sites are inventoried, hardened before deployment and monitored remotely.
Evidence: Deployed device inventory; hardening checklist; monitoring.

Rule: All stages, when a Infrastructure Vulnerability Scanning tool is named.
Wording: {{TOOL}} scans production infrastructure for vulnerabilities at least weekly, and findings are tracked to remediation.

Rule: All stages, when no Infrastructure Vulnerability Scanning tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Production infrastructure is scanned for vulnerabilities at least quarterly, and findings are tracked to remediation.

Rule: All stages, when a Software Vulnerability Scanning tool is named.
Wording: {{TOOL}} scans application code and dependencies on every change to production code, and findings are remediated within defined timeframes.

Rule: All stages, when no Software Vulnerability Scanning tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Application dependencies are checked for known vulnerabilities at least monthly, and updates are applied within defined timeframes.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Critical and high vulnerabilities are remediated within defined timeframes, or risk-accepted by management.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: An independent party performs a penetration test of the production application and infrastructure at least annually, and critical and high findings are remediated and retested.

Rule: All stages, when Penetration Test Approach is PTaaS / continuous testing or Bug bounty / crowdsourced.
Wording: A continuous testing or bug bounty programme runs year-round, and valid findings are triaged and remediated within defined timeframes.

Rule: All stages, when a Cloud Configuration Monitoring tool is named.
Wording: {{TOOL}} continuously checks production cloud configuration against a security baseline, and findings are triaged and remediated.

Rule: Scaleup and Enterprise, when no Cloud Configuration Monitoring tool is named (or it's TBC), and a Infrastructure tool is named.
Wording: Production cloud configuration is reviewed against a security baseline at least quarterly.

Rule: All stages, when Infrastructure operations is Self-managed.
Wording: Operating systems and software on self-managed production servers are patched within defined timeframes based on severity.

Rule: All stages, when a Audit Logging tool is named.
Wording: {{TOOL}} collects audit and security logs from production systems and retains them for at least one year, with access restricted.

Rule: All stages, when no Audit Logging tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Audit and security events from production systems are logged with native platform logging and retained for at least one year.

Rule: All stages, when a Security Threat Detection tool is named.
Wording: {{TOOL}} monitors production for security threats, and alerts are routed to responsible personnel who triage and resolve them.
Evidence: Detection configuration; alert history and triage notes.

Rule: All stages, when no Security Threat Detection tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Alerts are set up for defined security events in production (such as root logins and permission changes) and routed to responsible personnel who triage and resolve them.
Evidence: Alert rules; alert history and triage notes.

Rule: Scaleup and Enterprise. Always included.
Wording: An on-call rotation acknowledges and handles production alerts within defined response times.

Rule: Enterprise only. Always included.
Wording: Security logs and alert trends are reviewed and signed off at least monthly.

Rule: Enterprise only. Always included.
Wording: A security operations function, in-house or managed, monitors and responds to security alerts 24/7.
Evidence: SOC or MDR agreement; response metrics.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: An incident management policy defines how security events are identified, classified by severity, escalated and resolved.

Rule: All stages, when Incident response is Security-led.
Wording: An incident response plan makes the security function responsible for coordinating incidents, and is reviewed at least annually.

Rule: All stages, when Incident response isn't Security-led or Engineering-led (or isn't answered yet).
Wording: An incident response plan defines shared roles across security, operations and engineering, with a named incident lead for each incident, and is reviewed at least annually.

Rule: All stages, when Incident response is Engineering-led.
Wording: An incident response plan has system owners lead the technical response within defined escalation rules, with security incidents escalated to the security lead, and is reviewed at least annually.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Incidents are recorded, tracked and resolved by severity, and affected customers are notified in line with contractual commitments.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: The incident response plan is tested at least annually through a tabletop exercise or a real incident, and lessons are acted on.

Rule: Scaleup and Enterprise. Always included.
Wording: Significant incidents have a post-incident review, and corrective actions are tracked to completion.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: A change management policy defines how changes are developed, reviewed, tested, approved and released to production.

Rule: All stages, when a Code Repository tool is named.
Wording: Application code is kept in {{TOOL}}, and branch protection prevents direct changes to production branches.

Rule: All stages, when no Code Repository tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Application code and configuration are kept under version control, and production versions are protected from direct change.

Rule: All stages, when Change management is Traditional approval.
Wording: Each production change is recorded in a change ticket with testing and rollback details, and approved by an authorised approver before release.

Rule: All stages, when Change management isn't Traditional approval (or isn't answered yet).
Wording: Each change to production code is reviewed and approved by someone other than its author before it's merged.

Rule: All stages, when a Build and Deployment / CI/CD tool is named.
Wording: Tests and security scans run automatically in {{TOOL}} on every change, and changes can't be deployed until required checks pass.
Evidence: Pipeline configuration; required checks; run history.

Rule: All stages, when no Build and Deployment / CI/CD tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Each change is tested, and security scans are run, before it's deployed to production, and the results are recorded with the change.
Evidence: Test and scan records per change.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: Production is separated from development and test environments.

Rule: All stages, when Change management is Empowered developers or DevSecOps, and a Build and Deployment / CI/CD tool is named.
Wording: Only authorised developers can deploy to production, and deployments run only through {{TOOL}} from the protected branch.
Evidence: Deployer list; pipeline permissions; deployment history.

Rule: All stages, when Change management isn't Empowered developers or DevSecOps (or isn't answered yet), and a Build and Deployment / CI/CD tool is named.
Wording: Production deployments run only through {{TOOL}} from the protected branch, and pipeline settings can be changed only by authorised personnel.

Rule: All stages, when no Build and Deployment / CI/CD tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Only authorised personnel can deploy changes to production, and deployments are logged.

Rule: Scaleup and Enterprise. Always included.
Wording: Emergency changes follow an expedited process and are reviewed and approved retrospectively within two business days.

Rule: All stages, when a Infrastructure Configuration tool is named.
Wording: Production infrastructure is defined in {{TOOL}}, and infrastructure changes are peer reviewed before they're applied.

Rule: All stages, when no Infrastructure Configuration tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Changes to production infrastructure configuration are approved and recorded before they're made.

Rule: All stages, when Change management is DevSecOps.
Wording: Security gates block deployment of changes with unresolved critical findings from code, dependency or secret scanning.

Rule: All stages, when Service standardisation is Customised / managed.
Wording: Customer-specific configurations and customisations are requested or approved by the customer, tested, and tracked per customer.

Rule: All stages, when a Ticketing tool is named.
Wording: Access requests, changes, incidents and customer data requests are tracked in {{TOOL}}, recording each request, approval and resolution.
Evidence: Ticket history with approvals and resolution.

Rule: Enterprise only. Always included.
Wording: Significant new features and architecture changes have a documented security design review or threat model before release.

Rule: All stages, when a Backups and Recovery tool is named.
Wording: Production data is backed up automatically with {{TOOL}}, and backups are encrypted, retained per the retention schedule and stored separately from production.

Rule: All stages, when no Backups and Recovery tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Production data is backed up at least daily, backups are retained per the retention schedule, and failed backups are followed up.

Rule: All stages. Always included.
Wording: A business continuity and disaster recovery plan sets out how the company responds to and recovers from disruption, and is reviewed at least annually.

Rule: All stages, when Availability is in scope, and Availability responsibility is Committed availability.
Wording: Backups are restored and checked at least quarterly to confirm they're complete and usable.

Rule: All stages, when Availability is in scope, and Availability responsibility isn't Committed availability (or isn't answered yet).
Wording: Backups are restored and checked at least annually to confirm they're complete and usable.

Rule: All stages, when Availability is in scope.
Wording: The business continuity and disaster recovery plan is tested at least annually against defined recovery time and recovery point objectives.

Rule: All stages, when Availability is in scope, and Availability responsibility isn't Best efforts (or isn't answered yet).
Wording: Production runs across multiple availability zones, or an equivalent, so a single component failure doesn't stop the service.

Rule: All stages, when Availability is in scope, and Auto-scaling is Auto-scaling configured.
Wording: Production services scale automatically with demand, and scaling limits and alerts are reviewed at least quarterly.

Rule: All stages, when Availability is in scope, and Auto-scaling isn't Auto-scaling configured (or isn't answered yet).
Wording: Capacity and utilisation of production systems are monitored and forecast at least quarterly, and capacity is increased as required.

Rule: All stages, when Availability is in scope, and a Availability Monitoring tool is named.
Wording: {{TOOL}} monitors the availability and performance of production systems and alerts on-call personnel when thresholds are breached.

Rule: All stages, when Availability is in scope, and no Availability Monitoring tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Automated checks monitor the availability of production systems, and alerts go to responsible personnel.

Rule: All stages, when Availability is in scope, and Availability responsibility is Committed availability or Targeted availability.
Wording: Availability is measured against committed or target service levels each month, and breaches are investigated.

Rule: All stages, when Availability is in scope, and a Status Page tool is named.
Wording: Customers are told about outages and planned maintenance through {{TOOL}}, in line with service commitments.
Evidence: Status page incident and maintenance history.

Rule: All stages, when Availability is in scope, and no Status Page tool is named (or it's TBC).
Wording: Customers are told about outages and planned maintenance by email or in-app notice, in line with service commitments.
Evidence: Customer notices for outages and maintenance.

Values: On-premises data centre / server room|Colocation data centre
Rule: All stages, when Availability is in scope, and Facilities is On-premises data centre / server room or Colocation data centre.
Wording: Data centre spaces are protected by maintained environmental controls (power, cooling, fire suppression) that are tested at least annually.

Rule: Enterprise only, when Availability is in scope.
Wording: Production can fail over to a secondary region within the defined recovery time objective, and failover is tested at least annually.

Rule: All stages, when Confidentiality is in scope.
Wording: Confidential information is identified and labelled or recorded in line with the data classification policy when it's received or created.

Rule: All stages, when Confidentiality is in scope.
Wording: Confidential information is kept only for as long as the retention schedule allows.

Rule: All stages, when Confidentiality is in scope.
Wording: Customer confidential data is deleted when the customer asks or when their contract ends, in line with contractual commitments, and deletion is recorded.

Rule: All stages, when Confidentiality is in scope.
Wording: Customer data isn't used in development or test environments unless it's anonymised or the use is approved.

Rule: All stages, when Confidentiality is in scope, and Data minimisation is Minimised or Purpose-limited.
Wording: New features are reviewed so that only the data the service needs is collected and stored.

Rule: All stages, when Processing Integrity is in scope.
Wording: Processing specifications (inputs, processing and outputs) are documented for the service and communicated to customers.

Rule: All stages, when Processing Integrity is in scope.
Wording: System inputs are validated for completeness and accuracy, and invalid inputs are rejected or flagged.

Rule: All stages, when Processing Integrity is in scope.
Wording: Processing jobs are monitored, and errors are identified, corrected and reprocessed.

Rule: All stages, when Processing Integrity is in scope.
Wording: Outputs are checked for completeness and accuracy and are delivered only to intended recipients.

Rule: All stages, when Processing Integrity is in scope.
Wording: Stored data is protected from unauthorised change, and changes are traceable.

Rule: All stages, when Processing Integrity is in scope, and Responsibility for outcomes is Provider-reliant or Shared.
Wording: Outputs customers rely on are quality-checked against defined accuracy thresholds before release, and exceptions are handled.

Rule: All stages, when Privacy is in scope.
Wording: A privacy notice describes what personal information is collected, why, how it's used and shared, and individuals' rights, and is reviewed at least annually.

Rule: All stages, when Privacy is in scope.
Wording: Consent is obtained where required before personal information is collected or used, and choices are recorded.

Rule: All stages, when Privacy is in scope.
Wording: Personal information is collected only for the purposes identified in the privacy notice.

Rule: All stages, when Privacy is in scope.
Wording: Personal information is used only for stated purposes, retained per the retention schedule and securely disposed of.

Rule: All stages, when Privacy is in scope.
Wording: Requests to access, correct or delete personal information are verified, tracked and fulfilled within required timeframes.

Rule: All stages, when Privacy is in scope.
Wording: Personal information is disclosed to third parties only for stated purposes and under agreements that protect it.

Rule: All stages, when Privacy is in scope.
Wording: Privacy breaches are assessed and notified to affected individuals and regulators as required.

Rule: All stages, when Privacy is in scope.
Wording: Privacy enquiries and complaints are recorded, investigated and resolved, and compliance with privacy commitments is reviewed at least annually.

Rule: All stages, when a AI Models and Platforms tool is named.
Wording: AI models and platforms in use, including {{TOOL}}, are inventoried with an owner, purpose and the data shared, and are approved before use.

Rule: All stages, when a AI Models and Platforms tool is named.
Wording: An AI acceptable use policy defines approved AI tools and what data personnel may enter into them.

Rule: All stages, when a AI Models and Platforms tool is named.
Wording: Agreements with {{TOOL}} prevent customer data from being used to train their models, and only the data needed is shared.

Rule: All stages, when AI reliance is Assistive, AI-native or Agentic.
Wording: AI features are evaluated for accuracy, safety and misuse (including prompt injection) against documented acceptance criteria before release and after material model changes.

Rule: All stages, when AI reliance is AI-native or Agentic.
Wording: AI outputs are monitored in production for errors, drift and misuse, and issues are handled through incident management.

Rule: All stages, when AI reliance is Agentic.
Wording: Each AI agent acts only within defined permissions and boundaries. Consequential actions need human approval or can be reversed, and the boundaries are reviewed and re-approved when the agent's capabilities change.
Evidence: Agent permission and boundary configuration; approval workflow for consequential actions.

Rule: All stages, when AI reliance is Agentic.
Wording: Each AI agent operating in production is recorded in an agent inventory with its purpose, objectives, scope and boundaries, the systems and data it can reach, and its model and platform provider. The inventory is updated when agents are added or changed.

Rule: All stages, when AI reliance is Agentic.
Wording: A risk assessment is documented for each production agent before it goes live and when its capabilities change, covering what it can do, what it can affect and the controls that keep it within its boundaries. Agents are included in the periodic risk and control assessment.
Evidence: Agent risk assessments; risk register entries.
Tested by: Document inspection; sample of new or changed agents

Rule: All stages, when AI reliance is Agentic.
Wording: Each production agent has a named accountable owner who understands its role, monitors its activity and can restrict or stop it. Ownership is recorded in the agent inventory and reassigned when the owner changes.
Evidence: Agent inventory owner field; evidence the owner monitors the agent and can stop it.

Rule: All stages, when AI reliance is Agentic.
Control: Agent access authorisation and unique identity
Wording: Each production agent uses its own unique identity rather than a shared service account. Its permissions are approved before they are granted, in line with its defined purpose and scope, and limited to what its role requires.
Evidence: Agent identities and roles; access approvals.

Rule: All stages, when AI reliance is Agentic.
Wording: Agent and other non-human accounts are included in periodic access reviews. Each is confirmed as still needed, still appropriate to the agent's role and monitored by its owner.
Evidence: Access review records that include agent accounts.

Rule: All stages, when AI reliance is Agentic.
